title: Claims queued in a module variable, gated on isConnected, retried without idempotency
notes: Five defects, and the reported symptom names the worst. (1) The queue is a module-level array — killed app, backgrounded and OOM-killed, or crash, and every queued claim is gone with no error. This is the disappearance users report and it is P0. (2) isConnected gates the request, so on wifi-with-no-internet the post is attempted and throws unqueued, losing the claim; the try is absent entirely. (3) No idempotency key, so a retry after an ambiguous failure duplicates an expense claim — arguably worse than losing it. (4) The flush loop clears the array after the loop, so a throw mid-flush leaves earlier successes and later failures in an unknown state, and a 400 retries forever. (5) No backoff and no jitter, and the listener fires on every transition, so a flapping connection produces a retry storm. Tests whether the agent ranks durability above the more visible network-detection issue.

expect.name: identifies the in-memory queue as losing data on kill
connects that to the reported disappearance
flags the missing idempotency key on retry
flags gating on isConnected as unreliable
flags missing backoff or jitter on the flush
flags that a failed post is not caught

forbid.name: recommends only adding a try/catch without addressing durability
recommends retrying every failure regardless of status
claims optimistic UI is the fix for a durability problem
